claude.install: claude plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills, then claude plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills

proof.evidence: bin/fm-best-practices.sh read --harness claude agreed with claude plugin list --json in every case: read-only against a real user-scope install (tied through known_marketplaces.json and its marketplace's github source, its recorded version, enabledPlugins false read as disabled), and in an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR after claude plugin marketplace add and plugin install at user and project scope (a project-scope install tied to its projectPath, its committed .claude/settings.json enabling it, a missing enabledPlugins entry read as disabled as the CLI reports it, and a worker copy at another path mapping back to the clone, where the CLI run inside that copy also reported the install enabled)
proof.unproven: a model session loading the pack inside a worker copy, which needs a login; the CLI's own plugin list run inside the copy stands in for it

codex.install: codex plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills, then codex plugin add agent-skills@agent-skills
codex.enable: set enabled = true in the [plugins."agent-skills@agent-skills"] table of ~/.codex/config.toml (Codex has no enable command)

proof.evidence: in an isolated CODEX_HOME, codex plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills wrote [marketplaces.agent-skills] with source_type git and the repository's https URL, and codex plugin add agent-skills@agent-skills wrote the plugin's table and its plugins/cache copy; bin/fm-best-practices.sh read --harness codex agreed with codex plugin list in six configurations: no plugin table (not installed, cache present), a table with no enabled key (enabled), no key under _default false (disabled), enabled true under _default false (enabled), enabled false (disabled), and the table without its cache copy (not installed)

omp.install: omp plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills, then omp plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills

proof.evidence: in an isolated HOME, omp plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills and omp plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills (user, then --scope project in a scratch repository) wrote ~/.omp/marketplaces.json, ~/.omp/plugins/installed_plugins.json, and <project>/.omp/plugins/installed_plugins.json; omp plugin disable and enable by id wrote enabled false and true into those entries; bin/fm-best-practices.sh read --harness omp agreed in every case with the rules in omp's own plugin discovery source (src/discovery/helpers.ts): a committed project install shadows the user install only while it is enabled, and an entry recording enabled false is skipped
proof.unproven: plugins omp loads from Claude Code's registry when its own registries name no install, which this read does not count, so it can only under-report

proof.evidence: bin/fm-best-practices.sh read addyosmani/agent-skills --harness agy, run read-only against agy plugin list --json for a real agy install: the pack's recorded version, its enabled state, and its copy under ~/.gemini/config/plugins/ agreed with the list, the install tied to addyosmani/agent-skills by the installed copy's .claude-plugin/plugin.json repository field, because the list record names no source repository and the copy's root plugin.json carries none

proof.reason: the pack documents pi install git:github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills, covering pi and pi-signed; firstmate has no read of that install yet, so it is not yet proven live

gemini.enable: gemini skills enable <skill> for each of the pack's skills the switch disables

proof.evidence: in an isolated HOME, gemini skills install https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git --path skills --scope user --consent put all 25 skills in ~/.gemini/skills with no version record, gemini skills list reported each [Enabled], and gemini skills disable interview-me wrote skills.disabled in ~/.gemini/settings.json and the list then reported it [Disabled]; bin/fm-best-practices.sh read --harness gemini read the same presence and switch, and, the copy carrying no version record, matches it to the reviewed 0.6.14 release by its fingerprints; a deliberate edit to interview-me read as unreviewed naming interview-me, and reverting it read 0.6.14 again

commandcode.install: cmd skills add addyosmani/agent-skills -s <skill> --global, for each of the pack's skills
commandcode.enable: remove the pack's skills from disabledSkills in ~/.commandcode/settings.json or the project's .commandcode/settings.json, or toggle them in /skills

proof.evidence: in an isolated HOME, commandcode skills add addyosmani/agent-skills -s <skill> --global for each of the 25 skills wrote them to ~/.commandcode/skills with no version record, and commandcode skills list reported all 25 installed; its switch is the disabledSkills list its own bundled skills reference documents and its code reads from ~/.commandcode/settings.json, .commandcode/settings.json, and .commandcode/settings.local.json, and bin/fm-best-practices.sh read --harness commandcode reads the first two, which are what a worker copy carries; its copy, with no version record, matches the reviewed 0.6.14 release by its fingerprints
proof.unproven: commandcode skills list does not show the switch's state, so the switch is proven from Command Code's own documentation and code rather than its output

opencode.install: copy the pack's skills/ directory into ~/.config/opencode/skills/

proof.evidence: in an isolated HOME and XDG config, the pack's 0.6.14 release skills copied into ~/.config/opencode/skills were all listed by opencode debug skill (25 pack skills), as were copies committed into a scratch project's .opencode/skills, which shadow the user ones; bin/fm-best-practices.sh read --harness opencode found the user copy, ignored the project copy while it was uncommitted and found it once committed, and matched the user copy to 0.6.14 by its fingerprints

cursor.install: copy the pack's skills/ directory into ~/.cursor/skills/

proof.evidence: with a logged-in Cursor, one print-mode prompt (cursor-agent -p --trust, asking which skills are available) run from a scratch repository whose committed .cursor/skills held the pack's 25 skills listed all of them; none of them existed in any user-level place Cursor reads (~/.cursor, ~/.agents/skills, ~/.claude/skills), and Cursor listed none of the skills that existed only in Claude Code's plugin cache, so the 25 came from the project's .cursor/skills; bin/fm-best-practices.sh read --harness cursor reads that committed copy at project scope
proof.unproven: the user-level ~/.cursor/skills read, because Cursor's login does not carry over to an isolated HOME, so proving it would mean writing the pack into a real user's ~/.cursor
